discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-atom-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics (ultracold quantum gases)
motivation: After Bose-Einstein condensation was achieved, the decisive question was whether cold atoms could address the hard problems of condensed matter. Zoller and coworkers (1998) showed that atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Greiner, Bloch and colleagues (2002) observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, the first clean demonstration of a strongly correlated phase in a fully controllable quantum system. Bloch and Greiner then developed quantum gas microscopes, which image and manipulate individual atoms in lattices and have revealed antiferromagnetic correlations, many-body localization and string order. Their work founded analog quantum simulation as a discipline, now pursued in laboratories worldwide, including in developing countries. It changed which questions in many-body physics can be answered experimentally and opened a direct path to quantum technologies.
